endpoints.summary: Run rigid protein-protein docking. Returns a JobInfo; poll until completed.
endpoints.description: Run rigid protein-protein docking. Returns a JobInfo; poll until completed.

request_fields.name: num_samples
request_fields.description: Reverse-diffusion samples drawn by the score model (paper/upstream default 40). Runtime scales roughly linearly.

request_fields.name: actual_steps
request_fields.description: Denoising steps actually executed. Upstream uses num_steps=40 with an early-stop at actual_steps because the last few steps tend to overfit; usually keep this at 40.

request_fields.name: top_k
request_fields.description: How many top-ranked poses to write out as PDB (`dock_pose_<rank>.pdb`). The full N samples are always preserved in `raw_samples.pkl` regardless of top_k.

request_fields.name: use_confidence_model
request_fields.description: If True, run the confidence model to rank samples and emit dock_pose_<rank>.pdb by descending confidence. If False, skip the confidence pass (about 30 percent faster) and rank samples by their draw order — you lose the quality signal but save GPU time.

request_fields.name: seed
request_fields.description: Random seed for reverse diffusion. Leave None for a fresh sample each call; set explicitly for reproducibility. Framework echoes the resolved seed in JobInfo.input_params.
request_fields.default_note: random seed selected by the tool at runtime

request_fields.name: mirror_ligand
request_fields.description: Upstream option: mirror half of the samples (swap receptor/ligand roles) for extra diversity. Default off — enable only if you have a specific need for chirality-doubled ensembles.

request_fields.name: no_final_noise
request_fields.description: Upstream default: skip the noise term on the final denoising step. Stabilizes output; usually leave True.

examples.title: basic docking (40 samples, top-5, with confidence)
examples.curl: curl -X POST $URL/api/dock -F receptor=@receptor.pdb -F ligand=@ligand.pdb -F num_samples=40 -F top_k=5
examples.notes: Smallest useful call. Returns a JobInfo; poll /api/jobs/<id> until completed, then GET /api/jobs/<id>/files to download dock_pose_1.pdb etc.

examples.title: fast, no confidence model
examples.curl: curl -X POST $URL/api/dock -F receptor=@receptor.pdb -F ligand=@ligand.pdb -F num_samples=20 -F top_k=5 -F use_confidence_model=false
examples.notes: ~30% faster than the default. Use when you'll rerank externally or just need a quick pose sample.

examples.title: reproducible run with URI input
examples.curl: curl -X POST $URL/api/dock -F receptor_uri=oss://mybucket/rec.pdb -F ligand_uri=oss://mybucket/lig.pdb -F num_samples=40 -F top_k=10 -F seed=42
examples.notes: Uses OSS URIs (no file upload). Explicit seed gives deterministic sampling.

examples.title: FC async task mode (single 202 + blocking compute)
examples.curl: curl -X POST $URL/api/tasks/dock -H 'X-Fc-Invocation-Type: Async' -H 'X-Bioagent-Job-Id: my-dock-001' -F receptor=@receptor.pdb -F ligand=@ligand.pdb -F num_samples=40 -F top_k=5
examples.notes: Returns 202 immediately; FC keeps the instance alive until the diffusion finishes. Use this for production calls behind the FC async-task console toggle. Duplicate submits with the same X-Bioagent-Job-Id are deduped.

job_lifecycle.poll_recommendation: Poll the status endpoint every 5–120 s until status ∈ {'completed', 'failed'}. On failure, JobInfo.error_summary holds a one-line exception summary and error_tail holds the trailing ~4 KB of the subprocess log — usually enough for triage without a separate /log fetch.
job_lifecycle.restart_semantics: Jobs survive process and FC instance restarts via a `job.json` sidecar in each job directory. Jobs that were RUNNING at the moment of restart are downgraded to FAILED with failure_kind='interrupted'.

nas_layout.cross_instance_consistency: When multiple FC instances mount the same NAS at jobs_base_dir, all of them can see each other's jobs via read-through cache on GET. Writes (create/update) only happen on the instance that owns the subprocess.
nas_layout.cross_service_sharing: Other bioagent services mounted on the same NAS can read this service's output files directly by path, avoiding HTTP round-trips. Example: another service does `Path('/data/rfantibody_jobs/<id>/output/file.qv').read_bytes()`.

model.name: DiffDock-PP
model.note: Ligand/receptor terminology from EquiDock — both are proteins. Model is rigid (no torsion / no side-chain flexibility). For flexible or induced-fit binding, consider a co-folding service (AlphaFold-Multimer, Boltz-2) instead.
model.auxiliary_model: ESM-2 t33_650M_UR50D (residue embeddings; ~2.5 GB) — loaded from torch.hub cache on NAS.

tool_outputs.dock: output/dock_pose_<rank>.pdb (rank in [1, top_k]) — receptor + rotated/translated ligand in a single PDB per pose, ordered by confidence (descending). output/confidence_scores.json — the full ranked list with per-pose confidence values. output/raw_samples.pkl — all N raw samples (HeteroData objects) for reanalysis / RMSD scoring.

config_tips.num_samples: 40 is the paper default. Downgrade to 10-20 for T4 quick runs; runtime ~ linear.
config_tips.top_k: 5 covers most 'ensemble score & pick' agent flows without hoarding disk. Set higher if downstream will rerank with a separate scoring service.
config_tips.use_confidence_model: true (default) is recommended — the confidence pass adds ~30% runtime but gives you a ranking signal. Set false only when you plan to rerank externally.
config_tips.actual_steps: Keep at 40 unless you know you're compute-bound. Reducing below ~30 significantly degrades pose quality.

input_uri_schemes.job://<prev_job_id>/<file>: pipeline chaining (e.g. RFantibody or AlphaFold-Multimer output → DiffDock-PP resampling)
input_uri_schemes.file:///<path>: absolute path on the FC NAS mount
